title: Kingdom of Deira
capsule: Deira (Deren Rīce) was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom occupying the Vale of York and the East Riding of Yorkshire, roughly between the Humber and the Tees, founded in the mid-sixth century and associated with the dynasty of Ælle, who died around 588. Edwin of Deira (r. 616–633), baptized by Paulinus of York in 627 and acknowledged as bretwalda, marks the kingdom's political peak; his death at the Battle of Hatfield Chase against Penda of Mercia and Cadwallon of Gwynedd ended Deiran supremacy. Deira was thereafter repeatedly merged with Bernicia to the north as the composite kingdom of Northumbria, with the two kingdoms alternating in dominance; Oswiu of Bernicia permanently absorbed Deira around 651–654, ending its separate existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of Deira is identified from Bede and place-name evidence as the Vale of York and East Riding; exact boundaries with Bernicia and the British kingdoms to the west are not precisely documented.
